title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' notes. They study a combinatorial, 'tame' plane geometry. There is a poset M of 'constructible elements', graded by dimension: M_0 are points (vertices) and M_1 are open 1-dimensional pieces such as segments S_ab and edges. Two orders appear, a specialisation/incidence order (≤, ◁) and an order (<) along lines. 'Figures' and 'préfigures' are finite subsets of M, and supp°(Φ) is the constructible subspace they support.

The previous page proves a lemma on composing segments: for a<b<c, the family {S_ab, P_b, S_bc} has the same support as S_ac.

This page opens with 'Ainsi, le théorème est établi', closing the proof of a theorem whose part (b) followed by induction on card(∂Φ) from that lemma. Grothendieck then starts a corollary, 'détermination des supports constructibles de M', and crosses it out. The draft corollary reads:
- Every constructible subset is obtained by taking a flag of flags D = (T_1 < … < T_m) in Drap*(Drap*(L)), where L is the set of lines, and the associated piece F_D.
- For each T_i one chooses a set β_i of boundary points, β_i ⊂ ∂F_{T_i} = ∂T_i.
- One then forms Φ = (F_D minus its vertices) ∪ ⋃β_i, which equals ⋃_i((F_{T_i} minus F_{T_i}∩M_0) ∪ β_i).
- Finally supp°Φ is described as 'Omb°(Φ)'.

He replaces this with a sketched statement. Any such Φ can be replaced by a Φ' with the same support, obtained by 'resolving the crossings'. Φ' is 'non-crossing': for every vertex x in Φ'∩M_0, the number of elements X of Φ' with x ◁ X (x on the boundary of X) is at most 2, i.e. lies in {0,1,2}.

The next page then states the normal-form theorem. Every constructible subspace S is supp° of a unique 'monadic', later 'irredundant', prefigure P. S is the disjoint union of the open stars/cells amb°(X) for X in P. The 1-dimensional part P_1 consists of the ≤-maximal 1-dimensional elements of S. The 0-dimensional part P_0 consists of the boundary points of P_1 lying in S, together with the isolated vertices.

In modern terms this is a canonical minimal cell (stratified) decomposition of 1-dimensional constructible (semilinear/tame) subsets of a combinatorial plane. Crossing resolution corresponds to subdividing at intersection points, so the support becomes a disjoint union of open edges and vertices, i.e. the underlying graph is subdivided at crossings.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; the material is a sketch, and the corollary is abandoned mid-way.

The NB 'ce cardinal est alors ∈{0,1,2}' is only non-trivial if the displayed condition is something other than '≤2'. The symbol in the image is ambiguous, so the exact non-crossing condition is uncertain.
The 'resolution of crossings' is asserted without proof on this page.

ideas.what: Normal form for constructible subsets of a combinatorial plane: each is the support of a unique irredundant prefigure, written as a disjoint union of open cells.
ideas.modern_name: canonical (minimal) cell decomposition / stratification of semilinear or tame 1-dimensional sets; subdivision of a planar graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in PL topology; cell decomposition in o-minimality (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only calls for a 'tame topology' programme; this specific construction is not published.

ideas.what: Resolving crossings to obtain a non-crossing family in which each vertex is incident to at most 2 chosen edges.
ideas.modern_name: planarisation / subdivision at intersection points (arrangement refinement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in combinatorial geometry and line arrangements

ideas.what: Parametrising constructible pieces by flags of flags of lines, Drap*(Drap*(L)), together with chosen boundary points.
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial encoding of cells of a line arrangement (akin to covectors/sign vectors of oriented matroids)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketched, then abandoned, an explicit parametrisation of all constructible subsets of his combinatorial plane by flags of flags of lines plus boundary data. He replaced it with the irredundant-prefigure normal form on the next page. The parametrisation itself is not developed anywhere known.
missed.quote: on prend ... $F = F_D$, $D = (T_1 < T_2 < \dots < T_m) \in \mathrm{Drap}^*(\mathrm{Drap}^*(L))$, et pour tout $T_i$, on prend une partie $\beta_i \subset \partial F_{T_i}$
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It resembles combinatorial encodings of faces of line or pseudoline arrangements (oriented matroids). It could be compared with those as a purely combinatorial axiomatics of tame plane topology, though the significance is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a transitional, mostly crossed-out draft. Its content, a canonical cell decomposition and planarisation of crossings, is standard in spirit. The only mildly distinctive feature is the encoding by flags of flags inside Grothendieck's own axiomatic 'analysis situs'.
transcription_corrections: The page number at the top is very likely '107', not '67', given that the neighbouring pages are 106 and 108.
'Omb°(Φ)' may be 'amb°(Φ)', the notation used on the next page; the handwriting is ambiguous.
'Sup°' should be read as 'supp°', consistent with the neighbouring pages.
The relation in the non-crossing condition is unclear in the image (it looks like '≢2' or '≠2'); the transcription's '≤2' is a guess.
The word read as 'faisceau' is doubtful; it may be 'figure' or similar.
